# Chapter 50: Conformal Prediction and Calibration

> "A prediction algorithm should know what it doesn't know."
> — Vladimir Vovk, Algorithmic Learning in a Random World (2005)

## 50.1 The Calibration Problem in Healthcare

Healthcare AI systems must communicate uncertainty honestly.  A model that
says "82% chance of readmission" should be correct 82% of the time — not
60% or 95%.  Poorly calibrated confidence leads to:
- **Overconfident** predictions: clinicians over-rely on model outputs
- **Underconfident** predictions: necessary interventions are delayed

More fundamentally, most ML methods provide only **point predictions**.
A prediction interval [0.003, 0.011] for an access score is far more
actionable than a point estimate of 0.007.

**Conformal prediction** provides such intervals with *finite-sample
coverage guarantees* — without assuming any particular data distribution.

## 50.2 The Conformal Guarantee

**Theorem** (Vovk 2005): Under exchangeability of $(X_1, Y_1), \ldots, (X_{n+1}, Y_{n+1})$:

$$\Pr(Y_{n+1} \in C_\alpha(X_{n+1})) \geq 1 - \alpha$$

This holds for **any** regression model $\hat{f}$, any distribution, any
sample size.  It requires only the mild assumption of exchangeability
(satisfied when data are i.i.d. or under certain time-series conditions).

## 50.3 Split Conformal Prediction

### 50.3.1 Algorithm

1. Split data: training set $I_1$, calibration set $I_2$ (typically 15–30%)
2. Train model $\hat{f}$ on $I_1$
3. Compute **nonconformity scores**: $s_i = |y_i - \hat{f}(x_i)|$ for $i \in I_2$
4. Compute quantile: $\hat{q} = \text{Quantile}\left(\{s_i\}, \frac{\lceil(|I_2|+1)(1-\alpha)\rceil}{|I_2|}\right)$
5. Predict: $C_\alpha(x) = [\hat{f}(x) - \hat{q},\ \hat{f}(x) + \hat{q}]$

```julia
using ConformalHealth

# Any predict function works
predict_fn = X -> X * β_ols  # OLS, GP, neural network — doesn't matter

# Step 1: Calibrate on held-out data
cr = conformal_fit(predict_fn, X_calib, y_calib; α=0.10)

# Step 2: Generate prediction intervals
result = conformal_predict(cr, X_test)
println("Calibration q̂: $(round(cr.q̂; digits=4))")

# Step 3: Verify coverage (should be ≥ 0.90)
cov = conformal_coverage(result, y_test)
println("Empirical coverage: $(round(cov.coverage; digits=3))")
println("Mean interval width: $(round(cov.mean_width; digits=4))")
```

**Key property**: Split conformal produces **constant-width** intervals.
All predictions get the same ±q̂ margin, regardless of input.

## 50.4 Conformalized Quantile Regression (CQR)

CQR (Romano, Patterson & Candès 2019) produces **locally adaptive** intervals
that are wider where the model is uncertain.

### 50.4.1 Algorithm

1. Fit quantile regressors $\hat{q}_{\alpha/2}(x)$ and $\hat{q}_{1-\alpha/2}(x)$
2. Compute CQR scores: $s_i = \max(\hat{q}_{\alpha/2}(x_i) - y_i,\ y_i - \hat{q}_{1-\alpha/2}(x_i))$
3. Conformal adjustment: $\hat{q} = \text{Quantile}(\{s_i\}, 1-\alpha)$
4. Predict: $C(x) = [\hat{q}_{\alpha/2}(x) - \hat{q},\ \hat{q}_{1-\alpha/2}(x) + \hat{q}]$

```julia
m_cqr = cqr_fit(X_train, y_train, X_calib, y_calib; α=0.10)
df_intervals = cqr_predict(m_cqr, X_test)

println("CQR interval widths: $(round(minimum(df_intervals.width);digits=4)) " *
        "to $(round(maximum(df_intervals.width);digits=4))")
# CQR widths vary → locally adaptive!

# Conditional coverage in rural vs urban counties
mask_rural = test_groups .== "rural"
mask_urban = .!mask_rural
cov_rural = mean((y_test[mask_rural] .>= df_intervals.lower[mask_rural]) .&
                  (y_test[mask_rural] .<= df_intervals.upper[mask_rural]))
println("Coverage (rural): $(round(cov_rural; digits=3))")
```

## 50.5 Jackknife+

For small calibration sets where splitting is wasteful, **jackknife+**
uses leave-one-out residuals:

```julia
fit_fn = (Xtr, ytr) -> begin
    X_aug = hcat(ones(size(Xtr,1)), Xtr)
    β = (X_aug'X_aug + 1e-8I) \ X_aug'ytr
    X_new -> vec(hcat(ones(size(X_new,1)), X_new) * β)
end

# Uses all training data; no separate calibration set needed
jr = jackknife_plus(fit_fn, X_train, y_train, X_test;
                     α=0.10, max_n_loo=50)

println("Jackknife+ coverage: $(mean((y_test .>= jr.lower) .& (y_test .<= jr.upper)))")
```

**Guarantee**: $\Pr(Y \in C(X)) \geq 1 - 2\alpha$ (slightly weaker than split conformal).

## 50.6 Adaptive Prediction Sets for Classification

For the readmission classifier, conformal prediction produces **prediction
sets** — subsets of classes guaranteed to contain the true class:

```julia
# Calibrate APS on held-out data
# probs_calib: n_calib × K probability matrix (softmax outputs)
aps = aps_fit(probs_calib, y_calib; α=0.10, score_type=:aps)

# Prediction sets for new patients
sets = aps_predict(aps, probs_test)
df_sets = conformal_classify(probs_test, aps)

# Interpretation: set_size > 1 → model is uncertain
n_uncertain = sum(df_sets.uncertain)
println("Uncertain predictions: $n_uncertain / $(nrow(df_sets))")
println("Example set: $(df_sets.pred_set[1])")  # e.g., "1,2" means both class 1 and 2 plausible
```

**Clinical interpretation**: When the prediction set is {1, 2} (both readmission
and no-readmission), flag for clinician review rather than automated action.

## 50.7 Probability Calibration

### 50.7.1 Temperature Scaling

For neural network softmax outputs with overconfident logits:

$$p_k^{\text{cal}} = \frac{\exp(z_k / T)}{\sum_j \exp(z_j / T)}$$

$T > 1$: softer (more uncertain) probabilities; $T < 1$: harder.

```julia
# logits: n × K (before softmax); y: true class labels (1-indexed)
T_opt, probs_calibrated = temperature_scaling(logits, y_calib; max_iter=500)
println("Optimal temperature: $(round(T_opt; digits=3))")
# T > 1: model was overconfident
```

### 50.7.2 Isotonic Regression Calibration

For binary classifiers, isotonic calibration fits a monotone step function:

```julia
p_raw = model_probs  # raw probabilities from any classifier
y_cal = binary_labels

p_calibrated, cal_fn, _ = isotonic_calibrate(p_raw, y_cal)

# Check improvement
cr_before = calibration_error(p_raw, y_cal)
cr_after  = calibration_error(p_calibrated, y_cal)
println("ECE before: $(round(cr_before.ece;digits=4))")
println("ECE after:  $(round(cr_after.ece;digits=4))")
```

### 50.7.3 Reliability Diagram

A **reliability diagram** plots bin confidence (mean predicted probability)
against bin accuracy (fraction of positives).  Well-calibrated: diagonal line.

```julia
rd = reliability_diagram(p_calibrated, y_cal; n_bins=10)
# Plot rd.confidence vs rd.accuracy
# Perfect calibration: all points on the diagonal
```

## 50.8 Comparison: Method Selection

| Scenario | Recommended | Guarantee |
|----------|------------|-----------|
| Large calibration set (n>200), regression | Split Conformal | $\geq 1-\alpha$ |
| Heteroskedastic noise | CQR | $\geq 1-\alpha$, adaptive |
| Small calibration set | Jackknife+ | $\geq 1-2\alpha$ |
| Classification, K classes | APS | $\geq 1-\alpha$ |
| Neural net overconfidence | Temperature scaling | Empirical |
| Binary classifier miscalibration | Isotonic regression | Empirical |
